references.text: Pharaoh's command to throw all Hebrew male infants into the Nile explains why Moses was placed in a basket and why Pharaoh's daughter identified him as one of the Hebrew children.
The context of how the child was placed in the basket by the Nile, which led to Pharaoh's daughter finding him.
Stephen's speech in Acts refers to this event where Pharaoh's daughter took Moses and raised him as her own son.
Hebrews mentions that Moses was hidden for three months by his parents because they saw he was a beautiful child, and they were not afraid of the king's command.
Pharaoh's order to the midwives to kill Hebrew male infants provides the background for why Pharaoh's daughter immediately recognized the child as Hebrew.
Typological parallel: God's intervention to bring forth a savior figure (Ishmael/Moses) where the name or identity carries the message of God's attentiveness and compassion.
Clear contrast/parallel: Two women react differently to 'the Hebrew' – one with hatred and accusation (Potiphar's wife), the other with compassion and rescue (Pharaoh's daughter).
